title: GPU fleet deployment timetable by cloud zone — H1 2027
content:
Purpose and scope:
This sheet is a short-form operational timetable + capacity proforma for the GPU fleet rollout across cloud zones (NA, EU, APAC) targeted at H1 2027. It focuses on: allocation by cloud zone, expected node types by month, utilization targets, buffer (warm spare) policy, and gated rollout milestones. Intended audience: infra leads, SRE, platform eng planners, finance ops for commit sizing.

High-level summary:
- Goal: deliver a phased H1 2027 increase of ~28k GPU cards (aggregate equivalent) across NA/EU/APAC to support projected growth (hosted + dedicated) while preserving 15% operational slack for failover and maintenance windows.
- Approach: roll by cloud zone in staggered waves (NA -> EU -> APAC) with overlapping pre-warm windows. Prioritize H100s for high-throughput pathways, A100 for mid-tier, and a small MI250 pool for specialized int8 workloads.

Key assumptions (foundation for numbers):
- 18–22% month-over-month demand growth for hosted API traffic through Q1 2027, leveling to 8–10% in Q2 as Dedicated capacity ramps.
- Average active sequence length distribution remains ~120 tokens for gen workloads; peak tails still produce 2–3x instance token bursts.
- Quantization and batching improvements (Optimize) will yield ~12% effective token-cost reduction vs. baseline by Feb 2027.
- Procurement lead time: 8–12 weeks for cloud commit increases (reserved instances / capacity reservations).
- Target steady-state utilization per zone: 68% (NA), 62% (EU), 58% (APAC) with 15% buffer slack.

Deployment timetable (milestones and gating criteria):
- Nov 2025–Mar 2026: planning window and vendor negotiations (COMPLETED).
- Apr 2026: baseline runbook and pre-warm scripts validated in staging (SRE+Platform).
- Jun 2026: sign Dedicated commit NA region (pilot cohort). Rollout gating: 7-day latency SLO pass on pilot models + cost per token within 10% of forecast.
- Sep 2026: EU reserved capacity commit and canary rollout.
- Nov 2026: APAC soft-commit (cloud reserved window) to secure availability for H1 2027.
- Jan 2027: bulk capacity enablement (first wave goes live NA -> EU overlap).
- Mar 2027: scale to target capacity, begin capacity optimization pass (caching, batching, quantization tuning).

Notes on node_type and migration strategy:
- H100-80GB lanes are targeted at high-concurrency, low-latency hosted models. Where H100 inventory is constrained, fall back to A100-80/40GB with adjusted batching limits.
- MI250 nodes are a niche pool used for int8-heavy reranking and embedding dense compute; provision small hot pool in APAC and NA.
- Mixed lanes imply autoscale groups with heterogeneous instance types and elastic scheduling; runtime will pin by workload label.

Utilization policy and slack reasoning:
- Operational slack is held as warm instances ready to accept traffic without cold-start penalties. Slack target varies by region due to recovery time and capacity availability.
- Target slack: 15% nominal. APAC slightly higher to cover longer failover windows and regional procurement risk.

Risk register (top 6 risks):
- Vendor quota shortage (H100) -> mitigation: early soft-commit + fallback A100 lanes, pre-negotiated cloud burst rights (owner: Asha).
- Unexpected traffic spikes >3x forecast -> mitigation: autoscale overrides and global failover policy, telemetry alerts for immediate quota increase (owner: Liam).
- Cost overrun vs forecast due to extended H100 footprint -> mitigation: monthly cost review with Optimize team and tagging for model-cost centers (owner: Michael).
- Inter-region network constraints during failover -> mitigation: limit cross-region syncing, use warm-cold split for model KV caches (owner: SRE lead).
- Quantization regressions causing quality drop -> mitigation: gated eval suite + canary traffic limited to low-risk customers (owner: Applied ML).
- Reserved commitment timing miss -> mitigation: maintain short-term burstable capacity commitments and renegotiate with second-tier cloud partner (owner: procurement).

Operational action list (short):
- A: Finalize NA reserved commit and alignment with finance (due: 2026-06-10) -> owner: Michael Chen
- B: Complete EU canary runbooks and SLO tests (due: 2026-09-01) -> owner: Asha Patel
- C: Create APAC pre-warm checklist and local MI250 validation (due: 2026-11-01) -> owner: Sofia Martinez
- D: Instrument per-node telemetry for utilization heatmaps (due: 2026-04-15) -> owner: Liam O'Connor

Observability and testing notes:
- Must include token-level breakdown (model, system, retry) for first 30 days of new zone activation.
- Canary targets: 99th-pctl latency within commit SLO, error rate <0.2% on production traffic segment.
- Define a capacity test harness that can replay synthetic tails to validate autoscale thresholds.

Cost sensitivity snapshot (quick):
- Baseline blended cost per GPU-card-month (blended H100/A100/MI250) used for finance commit planning: $5,600/month/card (internal proforma).
- 10% variance in H100/A100 mix changes monthly spend estimate by ~7%.

Appendix: quick checklist for each zone activation:
- confirm reserved commit and billing cadence
- pre-warm nodes with internal traffic and run KV cache warm-up scripts
- validate rollbacks and fallback routing to adjacent zone
- enable SLO tracing and costs tags for new capacity
- run gated evals against sentinel prompts to catch quality regressions

Document versions and provenance:
- v0.1 (2025-11-12) initial proforma and assumptions
- v0.7 (2026-03-10) updated demand curves and early commit schedule

Open questions:
- should we reserve additional MI250 capacity in NA for enterprise ranking jobs, or rely on on-demand burst? (decision needed by 2026-07-01)
- confirm final token-cost targets with Optimize team after quantization program completes (ETA 2026-02)

If you want a CSV export for the month-by-month table or a printable checklist, ping me and I will attach a formatted sheet and the budget delta projection.
